key_insight: A falsification-guided, model-agnostic output protocol can outperform raw model scaling by enforcing auditable reasoning and termination discipline in hypothesis-driven decisions.
engineering_relevance: For deployed decision systems, the main bottleneck may be reliable output structure and verification workflow rather than model size alone.
method: Candidate × evidence matrix: every candidate checked against every evidence item
Require at least half of candidates to be falsified before final output
evidence_signal: On TCMEval-SDT (200 cases), the protocol rescued poorly disciplined models such as DeepSeek-V4-Flash (+0.267/+0.271) and reduced Kimi K3 run-to-run std from 0.218 to 0.007, while disciplined models saw a small accuracy drop.
watch_item: The protocol can incur measurable accuracy costs on already well-disciplined models, especially from the candidate-bounded formatting layer, so budget and task fit matter.
paper_title: Output Discipline Sets the Floor: A Falsification-Guided, Model-Agnostic Agent Protocol for Auditable Hypothesis-Driven Decision Making
